clue.text: Cleaner meandering outside university court showing disinclination for work?

indicators.note: the rearranged cleaner goes round the outside of the next pieces
the word cleaner wanders about, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cleaner wandering round a college quad seems in no hurry to get on with the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' looks like the person in the scene, but it is anagram fodder; 'meandering' gives RELANCE, which goes 'outside' the university and court pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwillingness or hesitancy to act is what the word means; the question mark nods to a lazy cleaner.

clue.text: Wild event sees one surrounded by rubbish

indicators.note: the word for one sits inside, with the rubbish word wrapped around it

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wild party ends with someone buried in litter.
explanation.definitionFit: A disturbance of the peace, or an uproarious occasion, is a wild event.

clue.text: Secure slab after skinning off its top

indicators.note: removing the uppermost layer of a down entry means dropping its first letter

parts.note: a block is a slab of stone or wood

explanation.surface: Instructions for preparing a stone slab: strip off the top layer to make it safe.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten something shut with a bolt or key is to secure it.

clue.text: Nothing left for possession by one American native or another

indicators.note: being possessed, held, by the native word means going inside it

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people of Canada
O, the round figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A dispute over something left to nobody, to be owned by one indigenous American or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one American native or another' gives CREE in the wordplay and, with 'another', the definition: a person of mixed European and African or native descent from the Caribbean or Louisiana.
explanation.definitionFit: A person born in the Caribbean or Louisiana of mixed descent is another kind of native of the Americas.

clue.text: Pain starts and needs to be dealt with — the answer must be drugs

indicators.note: dealing cards shuffles them out, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pain flares up and must be treated, so the remedy has to be medication.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes PAIN, STARTS and NEEDS (fifteen letters); 'and' only joins, and 'the answer must be' leads to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Medications prescribed for depression are a class of drugs.

clue.text: First sign of cuckoo and another bird will get fearful

indicators.note: the initial letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: a raven is a large black bird, another one besides the cuckoo

explanation.surface: Birdwatching notes: the first glimpse of a cuckoo plus a second species makes someone nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowardly person is fearful, lacking courage.

clue.text: Change from scheduled itinerary

indicators.note: the letters are taken out from within the words scheduled itinerary, spanning the gap

explanation.surface: A traveller alters plans that were set in a fixed timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise or alter text is to change it.

clue.text: Like a sort of insanity, in which one could discern loud aliens

indicators.note: the answer's letters can be made out, rearranged, within the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A madness in which someone hears noisy extraterrestrials, as the deluded often claim to.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also reads as a picture of the condition: someone hearing loud aliens is having false beliefs.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding fixed false beliefs is characteristic of a kind of mental illness, hence like a sort of insanity.

clue.text: One has four feet, is encountered in wild retreat

indicators.note: the met piece goes inside the scrambled letters
a wild retreat is disorderly, so the letters of retreat are scrambled

parts.note: met means encountered

explanation.surface: A four-legged animal turns up in a disorderly withdrawal into the wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' gives TETRAER, which the 'in' piece splits. The feet are metrical feet of verse, not legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of verse made of four metrical feet; the definition plays on feet as legs.

clue.text: Like some music that could excite Clare Short

indicators.note: exciting something stirs it up, so the letters of the politician's name are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A kind of music that might get a famously serious former Labour minister worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: Clare Short was a British Labour cabinet minister of the 1990s and 2000s. The online clue was replaced in the paper because its container gave one R too few.
explanation.definitionFit: Music scored for a full symphonic ensemble is described this way, so the adjective fits like some music.

clue.text: Note a piece of stage scenery

definitions.meaning: a note lowered by a semitone, such as B-something on a stave
a painted canvas frame forming part of a theatre set

explanation.surface: Remember a single item of theatre backdrop.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a semitone-lowered note in music and a framed scenery panel in theatre.

clue.text: Winner with female name drinks after victories

parts.note: a champ is a champion, a winner
Agnes is a woman's name

explanation.surface: The winner and a woman called by name share drinks after their wins.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparkling French wines are the drinks traditionally sprayed or sipped after victories.

clue.text: One comic off-beat, a learner becoming cheap

indicators.note: something off-beat is unconventional, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: An unconventional comedian, still a novice, turns out to be inexpensive to book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comic' looks like a person but is anagram fodder with 'One'; 'off-beat' gives the first eight letters, and 'becoming' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that costs little or saves money is cheap to run.

clue.text: Shelf aboard ship for land vehicles

indicators.note: being aboard means going inside the ship abbreviation

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: A shelf on a boat is swapped for transport on dry land.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleighs on runners are vehicles for land, especially snow, as opposed to boats.

clue.text: Hanging around to celebrate, having jumped over river

indicators.note: the celebrate word leaps over the river word, ending up on both sides of it

parts.note: to sing of something is to celebrate it in song
the Tay is a river in Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone lingers to party after leaping across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Remaining in one place rather than leaving is hanging around.

clue.text: One providing something to help a person sit up

definitions.text: One providing something to help a person sit up

parts.words: One providing something to help a person sit up
parts.note: sounds like a carer for an invalid, but the sitting up is on horseback and the something is a seat for a rider

explanation.walkthrough: 'sit up' suggests propping someone in bed; here it means being up on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesperson who makes leather riding seats provides what lets a rider sit up on a horse.

clue.text: Goddess shows negative emotion about the City

indicators.note: the emotion word goes around the City abbreviation

parts.note: hate is a strongly negative feeling
EC is the postcode area of the City of London, its financial district

explanation.surface: A deity is cross about the financial district of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek deity of witchcraft and crossroads is a goddess.

clue.text: Article about employment leads to a feeling of disgust

indicators.note: turned about, so the article is read backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
use means employment, putting to work

explanation.surface: A piece written about jobs leaves the reader revolted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article about' gives NA, and 'leads to' only links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sickness in the stomach, or loathing, is a feeling of disgust.

clue.text: Revenue from ancient tower? Cash coming with little effort

definitions.meaning: read literally, payment for a worn-out tow line, a tower being something that tows

explanation.surface: Takings from an old tower would be easy pickings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tower' is the thing that tows, so the old one is a worn rope.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means money earned for very little work, an easy profit.

clue.text: Fruit upset old man

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly man is distressed by some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The nut is botanically the stone of a drupe, a fruit.

clue.text: Daughter wants a facial disguise — here's the material

parts.note: a mask disguises the face

explanation.surface: A girl wants something to hide her face, and this is the fabric to make it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich patterned woven fabric is a material.

clue.text: Diplomat in shelter with hidden gun

indicators.note: the shelter word has the gun word concealed inside it

parts.note: lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
gat is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: An envoy holes up in a refuge with a concealed weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A papal envoy or ambassador is a diplomat.

clue.text: Character who hires something out?

definitions.meaning: one who lets property, read literally

explanation.surface: Someone who rents things out is described as quite a character.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a written symbol and, whimsically, one who lets out property.

clue.text: Silence brought by endlessly serious person trying to be funny

parts.note: to gag someone is to silence them

indicators.note: without its end, so the serious word loses its last letter

parts.note: stern means serious, severe

explanation.surface: A would-be comedian is silenced by a relentlessly solemn listener.
explanation.definitionFit: A joker or comic who tells jokes is a person trying to be funny.

clue.text: Audacity evident in kiss

explanation.surface: Bold cheek shows in a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both cheek or nerve and to kiss amorously.

clue.text: Cautious look up and down

indicators.note: the word reads the same going up the grid as coming down it

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone gives a wary glance, eyeing a person up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick furtive glance is a cautious look.

clue.text: Some grim Easterner, revolutionary ruler

indicators.note: revolving the letters means reading them backwards, as in a down entry going up
only part of the words grim Easterner is taken

explanation.surface: A grim-faced Eastern rebel seizes power.
explanation.definitionFit: A Muslim prince or commander is a ruler.

clue.text: Ordinary mother at home, virtuous person getting about in the morning

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
in means at home
ST abbreviates saint, a virtuous person
re means about, concerning
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: An ordinary mum, at home, saintly, going about in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Conventional and in line with general tastes means ordinary.

clue.text: Single game

definitions.meaning: a card game, a form of whist

explanation.definitionFit: The word means unaccompanied, and also names a whist-like card game.

clue.text: One in America with lots of stories?

definitions.text: One in America with lots of stories?

parts.words: One in America with lots of stories?
parts.note: suggests a storyteller in the USA, but stories is the American spelling of storeys, floors of a building

explanation.walkthrough: 'stories' looks like tales; in American spelling it means floors.
explanation.definitionFit: A very tall building, typical of American cities, has many floors.
